pros: Smooth performance: Offers a CVT gearbox which gives you a smooth and relaxed drive experience
Good features: Comes with an 8-inch touchscreen, a 7-inch digital driver’s display, a wireless phone charger, and a Lane-watch camera

Limited powertrains: No diesel engine on offer
Missing features: Does not get a 360-degree camera or a sunroof

pros: Light on the pocket: The strong-hybrid powertrain offers good fuel efficiency along with smooth and quick performance
Handles well: Even after being a big family SUV, it remains planted at high speeds with minimum body roll and feels stable around a corner
Premium interiors: The cabin is covered with soft touch padding and all plastics feel smooth and sturdy
cons: Less features: For its segment and positioning, the ZR-V offers less features than some Rs 20 lakh cars, and misses out on a few flashy pieces of equipment.
Limited space: While the rear seat offers good headroom and knee room, the lack of underthigh support can cause discomfort during long journeys.

pros: Feature-packed. Sunroof, Bose audio system, seat ventilation — everything that larger SUVs have.

Strong safety package: 6 airbags, 360° camera, electronic stability control, Level 2 ADAS and more.

cons: Top-end variants are quite expensive. Larger SUVs are available for the price.

Non-turbo petrol engine could have been offered with a CVT for budget buyers.

variant: Carens Clavis GTX Plus Turbo 6Str DCT
pros: Space. One of the select few cars that can accommodate 6/7 adults with relative ease.
The new design looks more SUVish. Full-LED lighting, 17-inch alloy wheels, roof rails add to the appeal.
Loaded with features: twin 12.3-inch displays, 8-speaker BOSE branded audio system, 360° camera, front seat ventilation, wireless charging — the works!
cons: ADAS is offered only with the turbo-petrol engine + DCT combination in the top model.
Features such as wireless Android Auto/Apple CarPlay and rear seat ventilation could have been offered with the top-variants.
No CVT option with the non-turbo petrol engine. Diesel-automatic is available in a single variant.

Segment best feature set: Panoramic sunroof, L2 ADAS, 360° camera, 30” panoramic display.
Rear seat space: a 6’5” tall person can fit behind a 6’ tall driver. Slide and recline function makes it super versatile.
390-465-litre boot space: on par with SUVs from one segment above. 60:40 split rear seats on offer too.
cons: Design is very unconventional which doesn’t leave a good first impression.
Fuel efficiency of turbo-petrol engine in heavy bumper-to-bumper traffic is known to be poor.
Ride quality is likely to feel slightly bouncy on highways.

Generous cabin space: Puts its wheelbase to good use, offering good leg space even for occupants over 6ft tall
Good feature list: Offers a massive 14-inch touchscreen, gesture control, a 360-degree camera, and ADAS Level 2 features
Easy-to-drive: Both petrol and diesel engines offer a smooth drive experience.
Comfortable Ride: Offers a good ride quality over bad roads and keeps the occupants comfortable
cons: ADAS is limited to the top-spec trim only
Polarising Look: Design, while distinctive, may not be to everyone’s taste. Styling may be too busy for some
Incomplete Powertrain: The lack of a diesel automatic powertrain feels like a fixable miss
Needs Physical Buttons: Even with the gesture controls, the large touchscreen is still not ergonomic to use on the move

pros: Comfortable & Handles Well: Limited body roll keeps the cabin stable and helps keep everyone comfortable
Great Features: Comes with a 12.3-inch touchscreen, powered front seats, a panoramic sunroof, and front seat ventilation and massage function
Premium Cabin: Gets leatherette padding everywhere and well damped buttons
Extreme Off-road Capabilities: Gets a four-wheel drive setup, three differential locks, and many off-road modes which helps it clear any obstacles.
cons: Not Exciting To Drive: While there is enough power for easy overtakes, it can feel a little slow to pick up speeds beyond 60kmph and it does not offer a thrilling performance
Needs Better Support: Due to the floor being raised, the underthigh support is compromised in all rows.
Some Missing Equipment: Could have benefitted with 2nd row seat ventilation, physical controls for headlamps, and 2nd row sunblinds.

Not an alternative to family-friendly sub-compact/compact SUVs that are more comfortable, practical, spacious and feature-loaded

pros: Usable performance: Feels peppy and returns a good fuel efficiency too!

Smooth AMT: Not as slow and jerky as regular AMTs.
cons: Misses out on comfort features like powered mirror adjust, rear power windows, reversing camera, driver seat height adjust and steering height adjust.
Refinement on highways: Engine gets noisy post 3000RPM.
Limited space: Not wide enough for three in the rear.
Rear seat practicality: No door pockets, cup holders or even seat back pockets.

pros: Offers feel-good features like sunroof, 360 degree camera and 9-inch touchscreen.
Ground clearance: 163mm is more than enough to drive easily over rough roads.
High mileage: Returns around 15-16 kmpl in the city in regular driving conditions.
Excellent boot space. Can store an entire suitcase set along with two soft bags.
Safety package: 5-star Global NCAP crash test rating and 6 airbags as standard.
Looks distinctive: New design elements give it an identity different from the Swift.
Comfortable ride quality: Cushioned over regular imperfections, and limits movement on sharper potholes too.
cons: AMT transmission: Slow and jerky on the highway, and upshifts quite early leaving less usable power.
Low engine refinement and performance: Feels dull with a full load and overtakes require planning.
Limited headroom: Sloping roofline limits headroom for 6-footers.

pros: Easy to drive: lightweight and amateur-friendly off-roader makes off-roading easy for amateurs.
Boot space: Usable enough for airport runs, even with all the rows up.
Attention grabber: Quirky styling, upright SUV stance, compact dimensions and bright exterior hues.
Spacious enough for four adults.
Ride comfort: Despite being a capable off-roader, offers good ride comfort in the city.
cons: Cabin Practicality: Lacks basics like bottle holders in the doors and no seat back pockets.
Engine performance: Adequate for the city, but feels underwhelming on a highway, especially with a full load.

AMT transmission feels smooth as long as you drive in a relaxed manner.
cons: Misses functional features like a rear view camera, day/night inside mirror and powered ORVMs.
Design is a hit or miss: SUV stance and cladding feels try-hard.

cons: Limited performance: 3-cylinder engine, while adequate, doesn’t feel as peppy as the older 4-cylinder engine

pros: Easy to drive: Small footprint, light steering, and light clutch make for a beginner-friendly package
Good Space and Packaging: Sliding and reclining second row, a removable third row, and tumble-fold seats give it good space and flexibility only a few cars have at this price point.
Comfortable For All: Absorbs shocks with ease, settles quickly, and limits body roll to keep all passengers comfortable.
Covers All The Basics: For a 7-seater priced less than some small hatchbacks, the Gravite covers all the essentials, including a good infotainment package.
cons: Feature misses: Equipment like auto climate control, a better quality rear view camera, and alloy wheels are sorely missed.
Modest powertrain: The sole 1-litre NA petrol engine offers average performance levels, and the low engine refinement can be irritating. Gravite is best driven in a relaxed manner.

pros: Good safety kit: 6 airbags are being offered from the base-spec variant
Premium feeling cabin: Use of soft touch leatherette padding on all touch points makes the cabin look and feel upmarket
Spacious cabin: For its price and segment, it offers one of the most spacious rear seat experience
Smooth drives: It has one of the best performing CVTs under Rs 10 lakh
cons: Small feature list: Still misses out on features like a sunroof, seat ventilation, and a big touchscreen
In consistent cabin quality: While the leatherette padding makes the cabin feel more premium, the flimsy AC knobs, and panel gaps have a negative impact on the overall cabin experience
Sub-par 360-degree camera: It has a grainy feed which is very hard to see in low light conditions
Less refined turbo-petrol engine: Vibrations can be felt in the footwell, on the steering wheel, and on the seats

pros: Attractive design: Makes the sub-4m MPV look modern and gives it a good road presence
Spacious and practical: Offers good space for 7 people (including children) and comes with loads of storage spaces
Good boot space: With the 3rd row folded, you have enough space (625-litres) to use the Triber for shifting houses
Good features: Gets an 8-inch touchscreen, a 7-inch digital driver’s display, and a wireless phone charger
cons: Feels underpowered: The 1-litre petrol engine leaves you wanting for more, especially when driving with a full load
Limited powertrains: Does not come with a more powerful petrol engine or a diesel unit
Missing features: Does not get automatic climate control, a sunroof, and a branded sound system

pros: Rich and ergonomic cabin: Leatherette dashboard, door pads, and steering wheel feel premium, and multiple physical dials help usability.
Great practicality: Adjustable front cupholders, big door pockets with a dustbin and umbrella slots, dual gloveboxes, rear removable storage box ensure more than adequate storage spaces.
Great highway cruiser: Sits at triple-digit speeds effortlessly with enough performance for overtakes.
Premium Features: Massaging and ventilated seats with memory function, 13-speaker Canton audio system, dual wireless phone chargers and three-zone climate control.
cons: Third row space: Only adequate for kids or pets.
Squeaking sounds from a few panels inside after covering 20,000 km+.

pros: Elegant styling: Individual elements in connected LED lighting and illuminated Skoda wordmark at the rear looks chic
Boot space: Not the biggest on-paper, but very practical in real life
Performance: Both 1-litre and 1.5-litre turbo-petrol engines offer good performance
Driving dynamics: Feels fun to drive without any big compromise in ride comfort
Value: Base variants offer a really good functional and convenience feature package
cons: No ADAS features could be a miss for people who do long intercity trips
Rear-view camera: Really poor quality and no dynamic guidelines render it almost useless in anything other than broad daylight
Powertrain options: No CNG, diesel or hybrid powertrain option for people looking for low-running costs

pros: Practical. Ample space for four 6-footers. Cabin storage is very well thought out too.
Enough features: Sunroof, ventilated and powered front seats, 10.1-inch touchscreen.
446-litre boot space is more than sufficient for 4 cabin-sized trolley bags.
Fun-to-drive: 1-litre TSI engine is fun to push hard and puts a smile on your face.
cons: No diesel or CNG options available.
Fuel efficiency isn’t great, particularly in heavy city traffic. Expect 10kmpl at best.
Minor annoyances: poor camera quality, very light horn, and noisy seat ventilation blowers spoil the experience.

pros: Turbo-petrol engine: One of the most affordable turbo-petrol cars in India, finally giving the Punch strong performance.

SUV-like design: Looks like a proper mini SUV now, with clear design cues borrowed from bigger Tata models.

Spacious cabin: Comfortably seats four adults with good headroom and legroom for the size.
cons: Touch-based air-conditioning panel: It is overly sensitive to touch and often requires you to take your eyes off the road, which isn’t ideal while driving.
No turbo-petrol automatic: The missing automatic gearbox with the turbo engine limits its appeal for city buyers.
Locked fuel efficiency: Our test cars had the minimum fuel efficiency locked at 8 kmpl, which is misleading and not transparent for the users
Interior feels familiar: Design changes are minimal, and plastic quality is just about average for the segment.

Wide opening doors and neutral seat height makes for convenient ingress and egress

pros: Effortless engine: The proven 2.8-litre diesel is torquey and relaxed, now paired with a smoother, more polished automatic.
Big cabin upgrade: A completely redesigned, chunky dashboard and a far more comfortable, big-person-friendly driving position.
Improved ride comfort: Toyota has taken a good amount of sharpness out of the ride, most noticeably in the front row.
Serious off-road hardware: Ladder-frame chassis, low-range 4x4, rear diff lock and a full suite of traction electronics.
Modern, imposing design: The redesigned face and brawnier stance look fresher and more aggressive without losing the Hilux's tough character.
cons: Under-equipped for the price: Manual AC, a manual-dimming mirror, fabric seats and no ADAS on a truck costing around Rs 35-40 lakh on-road.
Compromised rear seat: An upright, non-reclining backrest, a high floor and no rear AC vents make the back bench a poor place for family.
Still firm over big hits: Sharp speed breakers and deep potholes still send a strong jolt through the cabin.
Bulky in the city: Heavy low-speed steering and a 5,325 mm length make tight traffic and parking a chore.

Impressive tech package: Comes with a 15-inch touchscreen, a digital driver's display, and a HUD too

cons: Missing features: Does not get keyless entry, powered and ventilated front seats

pros: Sophisticated look: Classy, understated styling. Sporty GT variant on offer too
Strong engine options: 1- and 1.5-litre turbocharged petrol engines promise excitement
Great boot space: 521 litre boot is segment leading. 60:40 split rear seats bumps up practicality
Feature-loaded: 8-inch digital driver’s display, 10.1-inch touchscreen, ventilated seats, electric sunroof are among the highlights
cons: Limited powertrains: No diesel of hybrid engine options. City offers a strong hybrid powertrain.
Less rear seat space: Lack of width and strong seat contouring means the Virtus is best used as a four seater
